liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Not Fade Away** (2 reviews): Brent's B3 organ gives Not Fade Away a strong kick; The opening of this Not Fade Away is really good, coming out of Space [13][15]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Rare Morning Dew, reportedly only the fourth of 1982 and among about six or seven that year [12]
- **Greatest Story Ever Told** (1 review): Garcia is barely audible in the mix on Greatest Story, unlike usual [19]
- **Might As Well** (1 review): Garcia handles Might As Well with no problem [23]
- West L.A. Fadeaway sounds good and was an early performance of the song [12]
- West L.A. Fadeaway is described as funky [19]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd82-09-12 s1t01 Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd82-09-12 s1t02 Alabama Getaway**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd82-09-12 s1t03 Greatest Story Ever Told**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd82-09-12 s1t04 Friend Of The Devil**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd82-09-12 s1t05 Cassidy**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd82-09-12 s1t06 West LA Fadeaway**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd82-09-12 s1t07 Little Red Rooster**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd82-09-12 s1t08 Brown Eyed Women**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1982-09-12.144362.sbd.healy.streeter.smith.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 139 min [1]
- **gd1982-09-12.sbd.miller.114138.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 137 min; rated 3.6/5 by 10 [3]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sound is excellent [23]
- **gd1982-09-12.158702.senn.blend.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 140 min [4]
- **gd1982-09-12.122169.senn.streeter.miller.flac24**: source not stated; 19 songs; 144 min; rated 5/5 by 3 [6]. Said about its sound: Audience recording has top-notch sound, a welcome very good audience tape from this tour [22]
- **gd82-09-12.sbd.ladner.7826.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 135 min; rated 4.17/5 by 6 [9]. Said about its sound: Soundboard vocals sound excellent, with Garcia singing forcefully; Mix is crisp and well blended, with instruments balanced nicely, especially in the second set [12][17]
- **gd1982-09-12.135162.set2.nak300.schley.flac1644**: audience recording; 10 songs; 81 min [10]

## Around the show

- At the start of the second set's opener, Bobby calls out to the Rock Angels backstage [19]
- Reviewer says Not Fade Away was more of a groove tune in this era, before being paired with Throwing Stones [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1982-09-12.144362.sbd.healy.streeter.smith.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Dan Healy & Frank Streeter; transferred by Matt Smith, Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Dan Healy's Master Soundboard Cassettes (Sony TC-D5M/TDK MA-R90/dolby B)> Frank Streeter's 1st generation 1/4 track Reels @ 3.75 ips (Sony TC770/Maxell… [1]. Also: A Nakamichi CM300 source supplies two short patches, 0:09 and 0:26, in the Space into The Wheel transition [1]
- **gd1982-09-12.sbd.miller.114138.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Reel -> Dat -> CD [3]. Also: Re-master of shnid 7826, which had been wrongly labeled a cassette master; Joe B. Jones helped with pitch correction [3]
- **gd1982-09-12.158702.senn.blend.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Master Audience Cassettes; 2 x Sennheiser 441 mics + 1 x Sennheiser 421 mic > Sony D5; Jim Vita's 1st Generation Cassettes [4]. Also: A Sennheiser 441 source from Streeter and Miller supplies a 0:38 patch in Space [4]
- **gd1982-09-12.122169.senn.streeter.miller.flac24**: taped by Frank Streeter; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Sennheiser 441 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell MX90) [6]
- **gd82-09-12.sbd.ladner.7826.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [9]
- **gd1982-09-12.135162.set2.nak300.schley.flac1644**: taped by Brian Schley; transferred by Andrew F.; source: AUD: Nakamichi CM300/CP4 shotguns > Sony TC-D5 > Maxell MX-90. FOB recording by Brian Schley. [10]. Also: Drums section is patched from ID-122169, running 1:47 to 5:17; Don't Ease Me In seems to have been added to the tape from a different recording [10]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Ed Eguedelo: [Grateful Dead Lakeland Civic Center 1982 Concert Flyer](https://concertposterauction.com/Listing/Details/797398/Grateful-Dead-Lakeland-Civic-Center-1982-Concert-Flyer) [25]
- Poster by Gregg Nixon Grateful Dead: [1982-09-12 Lakeland Civic Center, Lakeland, FL, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1982-09-12-lakeland-civic-center-lakeland-fl-usa/) [26]
